course_description:
This course focuses on knowledge and application of research methods relating to cultural awareness and diversity in built environments and landscapes including understanding of Indigenous perspectives and cross-cultural approaches. Students will critically evaluate methods in stakeholder engagement, observational research and mapping studies to formulate propositions to meet identified social and environmental challenges with a focus on cultures and regions.

ARCH7094 is one of four Research Labs offered in the Master of Architecture program. Each Research Lab offers an exploration of the theoretical and methodological aspects of a particular sub-discipline within architectural research. Students will learn specific content through a series of seminars or lectures, and then develop a research project based on the theories and methods specific to this sub-discipline area.

ARCH7094 Culture and Place Research Lab introduces architecture related to Indigenous peoples andﾠplaces based on understanding place settings, approaches, theories and methods to generate evidence-informed solutions toﾠproduce a research report or essay.

course_aims: This course aims to extend students' understanding of research methods to address social and environmental challenges focusing on cultures and regions.

learning_outcomes.description: Conduct a critical review of relevant academic literature and/or architectural projects and proposals in response to a culture and place of indigeneous people.
Apply an appropriate strategy to undertaking research informed by cultural awareness.
Evaluate primary and secondary research evidence related to indigenous perspectives.
Independently and/or collaboratively formulate a research proposition that is grounded in indigenous cultures.
Independently prepare a research synthesis report/essay.

assessment_details.task_description: Assessment Rationale: This individual task requires students to develop their own critical reflections on lectures and tutorial learning task documenting and collating these into a research journal surveying research literature and other scholarly information each week. The reflective journal should cover informed understanding of core topics related Indigenous housing and cultures, place, place settings, well-being, energy and climate. Students will form in class small research groups (3-4 persons) to evaluate literature and critically discuss Indigenous social housing research covering national, state and different regional place settings in Australia. Students will individually synthesise their own critical summaries comparing evidence-based information from Australia, Queensland and Northern Territory on the following topics: Dimensions of Indigenous social housing, climate and wellbeing Australian, regional and remote geographies, place and climatic zones Either Regional townships of Gununa, (Qld) or Jurnkkurakurr/Tennant Creek, (NT) or Yarrabah (Qld) infrastructure settings Indigenous housing cultures, supply, needs and aspirations Culturally responsive housing design National, State and regional housing and population statistics Complex/Authentic assessment using AI and/or MT to support learning: This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) successful completion of assessment in this Course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of Ai and MT tools. Students with outstanding applications for extensions are advised to submit their assessment by the original due date, irrespective of whether the work is complete, so that what has been done can be graded.
Maximum extension is 7 days - this has been approved by the AD(Academic)
Late submission
The late penalty for this assessment item will be calculated as follows:
Standard 10% (or 1 grade) per day for 7 days.

assessment_details.task_description: Assessment Rationale: Undertake the design of individual social housing and climate resilience study defining evidence-informed methods to enhance liveability and wellbeing at a specific place. The final study scope and research question/s identified in Assessment 2 will be refined in your study using a combination of anonymised survey data, relevant literature and graphics. Note anonymised housing survey data will be provided by the Course Co-ordinator. The submission will present a critical reflection of the design of your evidence-informed method, identifying critical problems encountered in designing your study. It should demonstrate an informed understanding of Indigenous social housing and place combined with either wellbeing or climate resilience. You are required to include targeted graphic illustrations (e.g. climate modelling showing the attributes of the climate region) and population profile tables of a specific place/s. You should identify any potential constraints and weaknesses in your study method and relevance of anonymised survey data to your study. Your submission should not exceed 2,000 words (excluding annotated bibliography) describing your research method and critical reflection. You must include all Ai logged prompts, responses and refinements used in the development of your research method, understanding of the survey data or graphics that have assist you in your critical thematic analysis and graphics used to communicate your method.
